Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testToMapWithShortRecord` creates a CSVParser for the input "a,b" with a header of length 3 ("A", "B", "C"). The record read back from the parser contains only two values ["a", "b"], fewer than the header columns. The test then calls `toMap()` on this short record. Examining the source code, `toMap()` calls `putIn()` passing a new HashMap sized by the record's value length. The `putIn()` method iterates over all header entries stored in `mapping.entrySet()`, and uses the column index from each entry to access `values[col]`. If the record has fewer values than the header columns, then one of these column indices will be out of bounds of the `values` array, causing an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in `putIn()`.

This understanding directly matches the current issue report which states `toMap()` fails with this exception when the row length is shorter than the header length.

The root cause is that `putIn()` (and thus `toMap()`) assume that each header entry's column index is valid for the given record values array without validating bounds. Thus if the record has fewer columns than headers (which can happen in "short" records), `putIn()` blindly accesses an invalid index causing the failure.

No recent bug reports provide contradictory or additional contextual info relevant to this specific problem. Hence the diagnosis depends on the current bug report, the test, and the relevant methods.

To fix this issue, the `putIn()` method should check if the column index is valid for the values in the current record before calling `map.put(entry.getKey(), values[col])`, avoiding out of bounds exceptions when records are shorter than the header length. Alternatively, CSVRecord's construction or parsing could ensure the lengths always match, but the immediate fix is in `putIn()`.

This explains why the test fails exactly when calling `toMap()` on a short record and relates perfectly to the current issue report.
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.putIn(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>)
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.toMap()
